Core Concepts.title: Core Concepts
Core Concepts.description: Run npm i @hitgrab/finder in your repo of choice.

guides/context/index.title: Injecting Context
guides/context/index.description: Often, you'll need Finder to be aware of external context.

guides/context/injecting-context.title: Making Finder React components aware of external context

reference/api/events-api.title: Events
reference/api/events-api.description: The Events api can be accessed from finder.events.

reference/api/index.title: API
reference/api/index.description: FinderCore wraps Finder's internal methods to simplify the API surface.

reference/api/test-api.title: Tests
reference/api/test-api.description: Test lets you test a ruleset's results without mutating state. The Tests api can be accessed from finder.test.

reference/react-components/finder.title: Finder
reference/react-components/finder.description: The root component, Finder accepts an armada of configuration properties and provides an API context to consuming components.

reference/react-components/finder-conten.title: Finder.Content
reference/react-components/finder-conten.description: FinderContent accepts a set of renderProps, and will determine the most appropriate state to display. Only a single state can be active at a time.

reference/react-components/finder-search.title: Finder.SearchTermHaystack
reference/react-components/finder-search.description: This handy component allows you to highlight the segments in your haystack that matched your searchTerm. This wraps a StringMatch component and populates it with your Finder instance's current searchTerm.

reference/react-components/string-match.title: StringMatch
reference/react-components/string-match.description: This highlight string segment matches within a haystack.

reference/rules/effects/index.title: Effects
reference/rules/effects/index.description: Effects let you trigger callbacks when certain Finder conditions change. While you could also use an onChange event to recreate the same functionality, effects can be invaluable tools for complex forms with connected rules.

reference/rules/effects/rule-effects.title: Rule Effects
reference/rules/effects/rule-effects.description: ruleEffects are triggered when certain rules are changed. It allows you to couple rules to each other wihout adding complex onChange events.

reference/rules/effects/search-effects.title: Search Effects
reference/rules/effects/search-effects.description: searchEffects are triggered when the user searches for certain terms.

reference/rules/filter-rule.title: FilterRule
reference/rules/filter-rule.description: Define a filter predicate that will return a boolean for each item. If multiple filters are active, all filters must match for an item to be returned.

reference/rules/index.title: Rules
reference/rules/index.description: "Rules" are static definitions that tell Finder how to interact with the unique shape of your Items objects. Finder will use that information to determine what internal state to track.

reference/rules/ruleset.title: FinderRuleset
reference/rules/ruleset.description: Optional wrapper to ensures that an array of rules all have the correct shape.

reference/rules/search-rule.title: SearchRule
reference/rules/search-rule.description: Select strings from your items to search against

reference/rules/sort-by-rule.title: SortByRule
reference/rules/sort-by-rule.description: Only a single sortBy rule can be active at one time.

tutorial/controls.title: Build Form Controls
tutorial/controls.description: Finder doesn't have any opinion on how controls are rendered. Instead, it provides a useFinder hook that exposes Rule definitions, and state accessors/mutators so you can easily roll your own controls.

tutorial/filters.title: Add Filters
tutorial/filters.description: Filters come in three flavours; Boolean, Single value, and Multiple value.

tutorial/react.title: Display in React
tutorial/react.description: To use Finder in React, you'll need to use the `` component.

tutorial/review.title: Review Ruleset
tutorial/review.description: We've assembled our piles of rules. Let's bundle them using a finderRuleset type guard into a single file.

tutorial/search.title: Add a Search Rule
tutorial/search.description: SearchRules tell Finder how to interact with the searchable haystacks in your object. It can return a single string or an array of strings, and Finder will search them all.

tutorial/sort-by.title: Add SortBy Rules
tutorial/sort-by.description: We want to offer two sort options to the user; price and number of bedrooms.
